author: Barry Revzin

evidence.note: R0 used the spelling `do return` and considered `do_return`, `do_yield`, `do yield`, `do break`, and arrows as alternatives; R5 reports the switch from `do return` to `do_return` was made to avoid ambiguity, and R5 removed the implicit-last-value option that had been introduced in R4.
evidence.title: P2806R0: do expressions
evidence.what_changed: R0 proposed `do return` as the yield spelling and did not preclude an implicit last-value fallback, but the spelling was changed to `do_return` in R1 to avoid ambiguity with do-while loops.

evidence.note: P3549R0, on which P2806R2's divergence discussion builds, argues for treating always-escaping expressions in pattern matching and do expressions properly, and proposes std::noreturn_t to make diverging do expressions type-check; it references Barry's do-expression work and builds its rules on P2806R2.
evidence.title: P3549R0: Diverging expressions

position: Barry Revzin has consistently and publicly championed adding `do` expressions as a general, orthogonal statement-expression feature, with `do_return` as the keyword to yield the expression's value. Across revisions he has adjusted details under discussion rather than abandoning the core ask: R0 proposed `do return`, which became `do_return` in R1 to avoid ambiguity with do-while loops, and R5 removed the implicit-last-value option that R4 had introduced, keeping the design centered on explicit `do_return` yields. In the paper he argues that falling off the end of a `do` expression should be ill-formed rather than undefined behavior, and that escaping control flow (`return`, `break`, `continue`, `[[noreturn]]` calls) must be handled so the feature can replace immediately invoked lambdas and support pattern matching's use cases. The companion work P3549R0 he helped develop extends the same direction by proposing `std::noreturn_t` so diverging `do` expressions type-check correctly.
recommendation: The paper proposes adding a new kind of C++ expression, the `do` expression, which consists of a sequence of statements but is itself an expression with a value and type, and introduces a `do_return` statement to yield its value. It also specifies rules for type deduction, copy elision, control flow (including `return`, `break`, `continue`, `co_return`, and `[[noreturn]]`), scoping, lifetime, SFINAE-friendliness, grammar disambiguation, and where `do` expressions may appear.
title: do expressions
